title: Time-based geo surge pricing, entitlement controls, and billing visibility PRD
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement: Enterprise customers operate global workloads with predictable diurnal peaks and sudden regional surges. They want finer-grained controls so they can choose when to pay premium for guaranteed capacity vs. use lower-cost preemptible capacity, and they need transparent invoicing that shows time-windowed price multipliers and regional surges. This PRD proposes: 1) a time-windowed pricing primitive (price multiplier by recurring local time windows), 2) a per-region surge multiplier that can be enabled by account or route, and 3) entitlement toggles that let plan admins opt into guaranteed vs preemptible capacity for specific routes or models. The feature must surface in the Console (billing preview, per-route entitlement UI, and invoice line-itemization), in the Billing API (time-window and region tags, multiplier applied, and audit reason), and in metering exports (CSV/Parquet) for reconciliation. Goals: - Reduce support escalations due to unexpected surge charges by improving visibility - Enable customers to trade cost vs guaranteed capacity with clear billing signals - Maintain accurate metering and invoice correctness with full audit trail Out of scope: ad-hoc one-off discounts, marketplace billing integrations, dynamic per-request bidding engine. Assumptions: - We can rely on existing metering pipeline that tags requests with region and plan tier - Console has capability to render new billing preview components - Legal needs to sign-off on new invoice line item language
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Time-windowed multipliers: Customers can define up to 6 recurring local time windows per organization with a multiplier (0.5x-5x). Multiplier is applied at billing-metering time and visible on billing preview in Console.
AC2: Region surge multipliers: Admins can opt-in a region-level surge multiplier per plan; when active, requests served from that region include region_tag and applied multiplier in billing export.

AC3: Entitlement toggles: Plan-level entitlements expose two options per route/model: GUARANTEED_CAPACITY and PREEMPTIBLE_CAPACITY. Customers can map routes to entitlements and see projected cost delta in billing preview.

AC4: Invoice line items: Final invoice includes explicit line items for base usage, time-window multipliers, region surge charges, and entitlement premium. Each line item references supporting metering IDs and time windows.

AC5: Audit trail: Every applied multiplier must be recorded in metering export with fields: meter_id, timestamp, region, route, plan_id, multiplier_type (time_window|region|entitlement), multiplier_value, and policy_id. These fields must be present in CSV/Parquet exports used for reconciliation.
AC6: Billing API: Billing export endpoint adds new columns (time_window_id, region_surge_flag, entitlement_flag) and a calculation checksum. Backwards compatible: old fields remain unchanged.

AC7: Console UX: Billing preview in Console shows projected cost delta per-route when toggling time windows, region surges, and entitlement settings. Users can save configurations and see expected monthly impact.

AC8: Rollback safety: If metering pipeline fails to attach multiplier metadata for >0.1% of events in a 24h window, automatic fallback to NO_MULTIPLIER for that window and alert to SRE and billing team.
AC9: Contract & Invoicing: Legal-approved language added to invoice template explaining surge multipliers and entitlement premiums; invoices include a link to a customer-facing breakdown page.

AC10: Tests & Monitoring: End-to-end tests validate multiplier application across simulated time zones and regions; dashboards track multiplier application rate, invoice mismatch rate, and number of customer disputes per week (target < 0.5%).
notes: 2025-11-04: Initial scoping workshop with Growth and Enterprise Sales. Sales asked for optional per-route opt-in so they can offer guarantees on critical endpoints.

2025-11-18: Technical review with Serving Runtime and Metering teams. Major concern: attaching time-window metadata to streaming requests that span windows. Engineering proposed tagging requests at first token generation and storing window_id on meter batch.
2025-12-02: Legal review kickoff. Legal requested explicit customer-facing language and a one-click opt-out for surge-pricing windows for enterprise agreements.

2026-01-15: Design review. Console mockups v1 show billing preview and a timeline visualization for time windows. Design requests: show estimated savings and risk legend for preemptible vs guaranteed.
2026-02-07: Engineering estimate refined to 8 pts (backend metering changes 5, Console UI 2, billing export 1). SRE flagged the 0.1% fallback threshold as adjustable.
2026-02-28: Product review: prioritize region surge controls for EMEA pilot customers. Action: create pilot-specific defaults and enable feature flag gating.
2026-03-05: Added acceptance criterion AC8 (rollback safety) after discovery of edge cases with streaming sessions crossing midnight UTC.
